title: Recent homes sales in Greater Boston (July 29)
author: The Boston Globe
bullets: 430 Stuart St. #27D in Boston, a condo high-rise built in 2020, sold for $8.5 million.
57 Burnham St. in Belmont, a 2023-built one-family Colonial, sold for $2.109 million.
25 Haven Way in Beverly, a 1929-built Colonial on a large lot, sold for $5.3 million.

title: Olney: Red Sox have expressed interest in Marlins All-Star Otto Lopez
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox express interest in Marlins All-Star shortstop Otto Lopez before MLB trade deadline.
Otto Lopez leads the majors with a .331 batting average and 22 steals this 2026 season.
Boston seeks a long-term shortstop solution amid injuries and performance issues in current roster.

title: New Red Sox Curtis Mead lands on IL with broken wrist after 1 game with Boston
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Curtis Mead, a new Red Sox acquisition, suffered a broken wrist one game into his debut with Boston.
Mead was hit by a 95 mph pitch from Athletics' Jack Perkins, leading to his injury and placement on the IL.
Nick Sogard will replace Mead on the roster, with potential lineup adjustments due to the injury.

title: Watertown police shut down 4 bodyworks establishments after inspections
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Watertown police shut down four bodyworks establishments for licensing and occupancy violations after city inspections.
Thai Body Spa on Belmont St. was closed for possessing 'items of sexual nature' and lacking necessary permits.
The FBI and local authorities conducted the inspections, emphasizing a 'victim-centered approach' for employees.

title: Boston Shriners Hospital says it’s seeing multiple burn patients every week from this popular type of toy
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Shriners Children's Boston is treating multiple weekly cases of burns from gel-filled fidget toys exploding.
The hospital warns against microwaving the toys, which can cause severe scald and chemical burns.
Doctors report injuries from both body heat and environmental factors like warmth or extreme cold.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 4 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Kayshon Boutte has been standout at Patriots training camp, demonstrating skill with a 40-yard touchdown catch.
A.J. Brown experienced some timing issues with quarterback Drake Maye during practice, highlighting adjustment challenges.
Patriots saw setbacks at cornerback with injuries, as Carlton Davis and Charles Woods left practice early.

title: After local pushback, popular wildlife clinic moves on from ‘perfect’ Carlisle property
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Newhouse Wildlife Rescue is seeking a new location after Carlisle residents opposed plans for a wildlife clinic there.
Residents cited safety concerns, including increased traffic, as reasons for opposing the clinic's move to Carlisle.
The clinic had planned to purchase a 13.1-acre property in Carlisle, but will continue searching for alternatives.

title: Patriots’ WR Kyle Williams is staying upbeat despite limited training camp snaps
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Kyle Williams remains positive despite limited snaps in New England Patriots' crowded receiver room during training camp.
Williams aims to improve with offseason training focused on physicality and maintaining speed amid competitive roster battle.
Coach Mike Vrabel praised Williams for offseason efforts, noting his special teams contributions in last season's kick returns.

title: Boston is about to lose its last Boloco
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boloco will close its last location at 50 Congress St. in Boston on Sept. 25 due to property conversion plans.
Founded in 1997, Boloco peaked with 22 locations across New England and the Mid-Atlantic before declining to one.
John Pepper, co-founder of Boloco, repurchased the chain in 2015 but struggled to keep stores open post-pandemic.

title: Online and phone lottery games are now live in Mass. Here’s what to know.
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Massachusetts launched an online lottery platform allowing residents 21+ to play games like Mega Millions and Powerball on digital devices.
Retail exclusive games such as Keno will continue in physical locations; Mass Lottery Online includes strict identity and location checks.
Profits from online sales will fund early childhood education grants, addressing childcare affordability in Massachusetts.
